name: Myeloperoxidase Deficiency

criteria.description: Reduced or absent myeloperoxidase enzyme activity in neutrophils
Impaired microbial killing demonstrated by functional neutrophil assays
Identification of pathogenic variants in the MPO gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of reduced or absent myeloperoxidase enzyme activity plus recurrent fungal infections
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing and neutrophil functional assays support diagnosis but are not mandatory.

pathognomonic.notes: Most common fungal infection in MPO deficiency
Detected by flow cytometry or biochemical assays

common.notes: Often secondary to impaired neutrophil function

occasional.notes: Less frequent but possible in severe cases

rare.notes: Rare immune response to persistent infections

laboratory: Absent or markedly reduced myeloperoxidase enzyme activity in neutrophils
Normal neutrophil count with impaired oxidative burst
Positive fungal cultures from mucosal sites
imaging: Chest imaging may reveal fungal infiltrates in severe cases
genetic: Pathogenic variants in MPO gene detected by sequencing
other: Flow cytometry demonstrating defective neutrophil function
Histopathology showing fungal elements in infected tissues

distinguishingFeatures: Defect in NADPH oxidase complex rather than MPO enzyme
More severe bacterial and fungal infections
Marked leukocytosis with impaired neutrophil migration

redFlags: Recurrent or persistent mucocutaneous fungal infections
Severe or unusual bacterial infections despite normal neutrophil counts
Poor response to standard antimicrobial therapy
references: Newburger PE, Dale DC. Myeloperoxidase deficiency: prevalence and clinical significance. Ann Intern Med. 1982;97(2):239-245.
Aratani Y. Myeloperoxidase deficiency: prevalence, clinical significance and recent developments. Curr Opin Hematol. 2018;25(1):22-28.
Segal BH. Role of neutrophils in host defense against fungal infections. Curr Opin Microbiol. 2005;8(4):377-382.
